html:
Nitassinan, "our land", is the homeland of the Innu on the Quebec-Labrador peninsula of eastern Canada. The Innu are an Algonquian people, formerly called Montagnais and Naskapi by the French and English.

They lived by hunting caribou, moose and smaller game in the inland forest and taiga, and fishing salmon and seals on the coast of the St. Lawrence in summer. They travelled by canoe and snowshoe in family bands. Their language is close to that of the Cree.

The Innu met Basque whalers in the 1500s and became partners of the French fur trade at Tadoussac, the first trading post of New France. In the 1900s mines, hydro dams and low-level military flights from Goose Bay reached deep into Nitassinan, and the Innu protested against them. Groups within it include the Montagnais and the Naskapi. See also Innu.
